question.text: Nilgiri Credit Opportunities Fund (Cat II) has a 7-member Investment Committee (IC): 4 members are employees of the Manager, and 3 are external independent members nominated by the large anchor LPs. For a specific INR 150 crore investment decision, the PPM requires investor consent from external IC members. What consent threshold must be met per SEBI's IC governance rules for Cat I/II AIFs (unless the investor qualifies for the INR 70 crore waiver)?

answer.text: Simple majority of external members (2 out of 3)
At least 75% of the external IC members must consent
Unanimous consent of ALL IC members (internal and external combined)
External members have no voting rights — they are only observers

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI's framework on IC governance for Cat I/II AIFs where external members are part of the IC, consent from at least 75% of the external members of the IC is required for investment decisions, AND every investor of the AIF whose commitment is below the waiver threshold (INR 70 crore) must provide consent. For very large LPs (commitment >= INR 70 crore) who sign a formal waiver, the investor consent requirement is waived. The Trap: Simple majority understates the threshold. Unanimous-of-all overstates. The observer-only option is wrong — external IC members are typically voting members for governance legitimacy. The INR 70 crore figure is a waiver threshold — commonly confused with a sponsor contribution or corpus threshold. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 75%+INR 70 cr waiver mechanic. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests it from LP-rights-disclosure angle. Note: this is a Cat I/II-specific governance feature — not relevant to XIX-B/XIX-E Cat III contexts. Manager's Pro-Tip: When drafting the IC charter, document (a) voting thresholds, (b) recusal rules for conflicts, (c) the INR 70 cr waiver letter template. LPs >= INR 70 cr typically sign the waiver at subscription; keep a signed waiver register to avoid consent-delay risk on hot deals.
